milestone: IRL Stewardship — Access Maintenance + Research Persona Legibility + Capability-Scoped Participation shipped and merged to dev (branch claude/irl-stewardship-access-capability, commits 505097826..c9abcc9a7). Filed at close-out per CLAUDE.md's Resolution -> Invariant Loop, triggers #7 (a successful implementation established a reusable pattern) and #8 (a milestone became demonstrably complete).
problem: A new caller-resolution gate for the steward participation routes (app/api/steward/participation/_lib/resolveStewardAuthority.ts) was first written with an ad hoc '{ error }' failure shape instead of matching the shape every other caller-resolution gate in this codebase already uses.
observedFailure: resolveStewardAuthority's first draft returned a bespoke '{ error: string }' object on failure, distinct from the shape its sibling gates (requireChannelAccess, requireReviewAccess) already return.

tests/persona-spine-fetch.test.ts (a canary that greps for gate-shape drift across spine-aware routes) caught the mismatch, forcing a refactor of five already-written route files (app/api/steward/participation/route.ts, grants/[grantId]/route.ts, capabilities/route.ts, capabilities/[capabilityId]/route.ts, research-persona/route.ts) plus the gate itself and two test canaries, after the routes had already been written against the wrong shape.
rootCauses: No single documented convention named the expected shape of a caller-resolution gate before this route was written, so the natural-seeming '{ error }' shape was chosen locally instead of being checked against precedent first.
The mismatch was only caught downstream, by a canary scanning for a different concern (spine-fetch discipline), rather than by any explicit rule an author could consult while first writing the gate.
resolution: resolveStewardAuthority (app/api/steward/participation/_lib/resolveStewardAuthority.ts) now returns exactly '{ ok: true, personaId, authority, admin } | { ok: false, response }', matching requireChannelAccess and requireReviewAccess's own established shape verbatim -- 'response' is a ready-to-return NextResponse, never a raw error string a caller must re-wrap.

All five steward-participation route files were refactored to destructure this shape and 'return gate.response' directly on failure, removing the bespoke error-to-NextResponse translation each route had begun writing independently.

tests/irl-stewardship-access-capability.test.ts includes one explicit shape-parity check asserting resolveStewardAuthority's failure branch matches the sibling gates' shape, so a future regression is caught at the gate's own test, not only downstream in an unrelated canary.
rejectedApproaches: Leaving the bespoke '{ error }' shape in place and having each route translate it locally -- rejected once tests/persona-spine-fetch.test.ts flagged the drift, since it would have meant five call sites each carrying their own translation logic for the same gate, and a fourth or fifth future steward route repeating the same mistake.
